newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks decline by lunch on lack of confidence.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks decline by lunch on lack of confidence.

text.p: A lack of confidence and economic worries prompted investors to unload stocks and drive the index down in thin trade by the lunch break on Friday, brokers said.

"Investors sold almost across the board as they lacked confidence in the market. They're also worried about the country's economy, especially (July) foreign reserves which they believed would be weaker than the June figures," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
The composite SET index was 10.66 points lower at 654.96 on 1.5 billion baht turnover by lunch.
June foreign reserves stood at $32.4 billion, down from $33.3 billion in May. The figures were above market expectations.
Brokers said the market was not active because investors were also awaiting for inflation figures to be released by the commerce ministry later in the day.

Eastern Water Resources Development and Management Plc, debuted earlier this week, topped the active list, rising four baht to 48.50. Siam Commercial Bank lost one to 135 and National Finance shed two to 34.
